verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Stagehand caches `act()`, `observe()` and `extract()` results to cut LLM cost and speed up runs, and that actions keep recorded selectors that `selfHeal` can re-infer when they break. A v3 guide describes auto-caching that turns agent-discovered workflows into deterministic scripts running 10-100x faster. Community comments that Stagehand regenerates actions on every run come from an early launch thread and predate the caching docs, so they don't concretely contradict them. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on confirmation that cached replays are deterministic and cheaper; cache configuration and invalidation details are thin; v4 caching is described as server-side, so local or self-hosted caching is unclear; the deterministic-script guide is v3-only.
